svg.title: One UUIDv7, six representations
svg.desc: @anizoptera/uuid-slug: one UUIDv7 in six forms that all convert back to the same UUID. UUID text 0198abcd-1234-7abc-9def-0123456789ab; 16 bytes; plain base64url AZirzRI0eryd7wEjRWeJqw (39% shorter than UUID text); plain base32hex 06canj8i6htbp7ff04hkaps9lc (28% shorter than UUID text, sorts by time); masked base64url ap225Qa_y6wN5LQCJgwH0z and masked base32hex daerdp86nv5qo3f4mg12c307qco hide the UUID's time and fields and decode with your key. Flipping one UUID bit changes 22 of 22 masked base64url characters (hAHeRPmJFqjOuXUQnhljgb).
svg.text: Store the UUID. Every form below converts back to it exactly; masked forms need your custom key.
36 characters as text · 16 bytes in binary
Great for UUID columns and UUID-only APIs.
The standard form: every database and UUID library accepts it.
Great for binary storage and transport.
Writes into your buffer; on error the buffer stays unchanged.
PLAIN SLUGS · any UUID · no key · the same 128 bits in fewer characters
Great for text storage and transport: URLs, logs, JSON.
Any base64url decoder returns its 16 UUID bytes.
Great for case-insensitive filenames and time-sorted text keys.
28% shorter than UUID text; time-range queries work on the ID itself.
MASKED SLUGS · UUIDv7 only · need the matching key
Examples use the public demo key
Your key scrambles all UUID bits, so the slug shows no time or fields. The key turns it back into the same UUID.
Inside: 42-bit time (~139 years from 1970, or from an optional start date you set) + 74 payload bits + 16-bit check.
Plain and masked base64url look alike. Decode each with the function for the form you issued.
Great for public URLs and APIs: text transport that hides the UUID.
Decoding needs the key that made it: keep old keys,
Great for masked IDs in case-insensitive filenames.
25% shorter than UUID text. Same UUID + same key = same slug.
One codec decodes both masked forms.
Last UUID byte · flip one bit
¹ UUIDv7: sorts by creation millisecond if all IDs share one case and alphabet; not event order within a millisecond.
² Text order follows creation time for most IDs. For exact time order, use base32hex.
Compare decoded UUIDs, not strings: one UUID has many valid spellings.
A wrong key passes the check about 1 time in 65,536 and returns a wrong UUID. Masking is not strong or secure encryption.
